sentences.text: The appellant has filed the present appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act being aggrieved by the award dated 25.11.2019 passed in Claim Case No.13/2016 whereby challenging the quantum of compensation on the ground that inadequate amount has been awarded even though the appellant has suffered permanent disability.
2. The liability of the insurance company is not under dispute.

3. The facts relevant for the purpose of the present case are that on 04.01.2016 at around 04:00 during the day, the appellant was going along with his father-in-law from Bank of India to Anand Jewelers on foot.
At that time, motorcycle number MP41-MU-5117 came from wrong side and dashed into the appellant because of which he sustained grievous injuries into his 2 MA-1421-2020 left leg.
The rider of the bike was riding the same in a rash and negligent manner.
He was taken to Bafna Hospital, Indore where fracture in his tibia fibula bone of left leg was found and implant of rod was inserted into his left leg.
He remained hospitalized for 7 days.
4. The appellant filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him.
He claimed before the claims tribunal that he has sustained permanent disability to the extent of 25% which he demonstrated by exhibiting permanent disability certificate Ex.P-49.

In support of the same, statements of medical expert Dr.
Rajesh Dashore PW-2 were also recorded.

The claims tribunal considering that the doctor has suggested that there is shortening of left leg due to the injuries sustained by the appellant opined that he has suffered 25% permanent disability into his left leg.
The claims tribunal without considering this aspect has concluded that there is no loss of earning capacity and has awarded only an amount of Rs.65,049/- for loss of earning during treatment.
This is the grievance of the appellant in the present case.

He also submits that meager amount has been awarded as for special diet on amount of Rs.3000/- has been awarded; for transportation only Rs.700/- has been awarded and for Virendra vs Pawan Choubey on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165039839/

has been awarded.
He thus prays for enhancement of compensation.

5. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/insurance company supports the findings of the award by referring to the findings recorded recorded by the claims tribunal in para 10 and 11 of the impugned award.

He submits that the claims tribunal has properly assigned reasons for not 3 MA-1421-2020 awarding compensation for permanent disability as there was no loss of earning capacity looking to the nature of work which the appellant was doing.
He was working as a property broker.
As such, the claims tribunal found that there was no loss of earning capacity.

Learned counsel placed reliance upon the judgment delivered by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Rajkumar vs. Ajay Mehra and Others in Civil Appeal No.8981 of 2010 (arising out of SLP (C)
No.10383 of 2007) and submits that the claims tribunal has correctly applied the test of functional disability, hence, no interference is warranted with the impugned award.
6. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
7.

sentences.text: From perusal of Ex.P-49, permanent disability certificate and the statement of the doctor, this Court is of the considered view that although this cannot be denied that the appellant has suffered injuries and consequential hospitalization, insertion of implant, however, a close scrutiny of the findings recorded by the claims tribunal in para 11 would show that the claims tribunal has properly applied the test of functional disability.
The appellant has not been able to demonstrate before this Court and even before the tribunal that the injury has caused any interference in his work.
There is no demonstration of the fact that he suffered any loss of earning capacity.

8. However, the amount as has been awarded by the claims tribunal in various heads like special diet, transportation, attendant and even for pain and suffering appears to be meager considering the fact that there was hospitalisation for a period of 7 days and insertion of implant into the left lower limb.
It is also seen that although the claims tribunal accepted the grievous injuries suffered by the appellant but nothing has been awarded for sustaining grievous injuries.
As such 4 MA-1421-2020 an amount of Rs.75,000/-, in lump-sum, is hereby awarded to the appellant over and above the amount already awarded by the claims tribunal.
This enhanced amount shall carry interest @6% per annum from the date of application before the claims tribunal.
9. With the aforesaid, the present appeal stands disposed of.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE N.R.
